description.narrative: Contributes to a situation where people living in poverty are empowered to contribute to the realization of their development rights and their potential to break out of poverty

policy-marker.narrative: The ASC programme partners with various community-based groups (CBGs) and networks as entry points into the communities. ADRA builds the capacity of these formal and informal CBGs and networks, including multiple youth clubs, to have strong, functional, inclusive and gender sensitive organisational structures, enabling them to better identify and voice their concerns on behalf of the group or the community at large. ADRA promotes gender equality and the rights of marginalised groups, particularly women, through the streamlining of gender in programme activities. ADRA also works with religious and traditional leaders and builds their capacity to identify and understand the effects of negative social norms that affect the participation of people living in poverty, as well as work with such leaders to promote, enforce and advocate for changing negative social norms/beliefs.

title.narrative: Change Area A: Communities articulate concerns and claim their rights

description.narrative: The theory of change is that if people know their rights, if they are organised, if issues of concern to people living in poverty are raised publicly, then relevant decision makers will be more motivated to address these issues and find solutions to the needs and concerns raised.

title.narrative: # of CBOs/ networks actively involved in advocacy initiatives

description.narrative: During the course of 2018, 36 out of 93 CBOs/networks in Uganda and 8 out of 41 CBOs/networks in Malawi were actively involved in advocacy initiatives.

title.narrative: # of advocacy issues identified by CBOs/networks are broadcasted/printed/raised at local or national media platforms

description.narrative: During the course of the year a total of 14 issues were identified and broadcasted over two local radio stations in Uganda and Status of Indicator by end of year 5 advocacy issues were identified and raised to local or national platforms in Malawi.
